prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1362; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer responded to a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. Driver 1 and a Passenger were in the vehicle at the scene, and a bystander who arrived shortly afterward confirmed they had been seated inside. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and said the impact pushed them forward and back against the seat. The damage to both front ends is consistent with a low-speed frontal impact, and the reported injuries are the kind one would expect from that force. Several older scratches along the lower bumper of Driver 1's vehicle may predate this collision and were noted separately. No independent witness saw the collision itself, and no photographs of the scene or vehicles were submitted by anyone other than the officer. No other crash report was located for either location. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy card found in the vehicle. Both drivers were cooperative, and no citations were issued at the scene.
